question: White sand and window glass are both mostly silica. Why is sand opaque?
options: Light scatters off countless grain surfaces
Its atoms are arranged in crystals
answer: Light scatters off countless grain surfaces. Each boundary between silica and air bends and reflects a little light, and after thousands of them nothing passes straight through. Crystals are not the reason: a single quartz crystal is clear. Crush a clear pane and the heap turns white too, as clear ice turns into white snow.
move: When two things differ in several ways, test each difference separately.
trap: Crystal versus glass is the famous difference, so it must be the cause.
reference: Bohren & Huffman, Absorption and Scattering of Light by Small Particles, Wiley, 1983
